instructions: Melt the butter in a medium pot over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, until it darkens a shade.
Add the minced garlic and mint. Stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes, broth, sugar, salt and pepper. Turn the heat to high and bring it to a boil, then turn it down to medium-low and simmer for 8 minutes.
Break the vermicelli into short pieces and add it. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring once or twice, until tender. If the soup gets too thick, stir in a splash of water.
Take the pot off the heat. Stir in the chopped parsley and a squeeze of lemon.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rest of the lemon cut in wedges.
method_notes: Cooking Gorgeous (5 out of 5 from 1 vote, so below the 20 ratings needed) builds the soup on butter, tomato paste, mint and stock, with lemon and parsley at the end. It uses orzo; this uses thin vermicelli, which cooks in about 5 minutes. Turkish Food and Recipes' tomato soup with vermicelli adds crushed tomato and a little sugar, which give it a fuller tomato body, so those are borrowed. The red pepper paste and chili are left out so it stays mild for kids.
